The maximum value is $1+\sqrt3-\sqrt{2\sqrt3}\approx 0.871$. The derivation follows.

Place $O$ at the origin with $OX$ along the positive $x$-axis and $OY$ along the positive $y$-axis. Then $P=\left(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2},\tfrac12\right)$.

Triangle $OMN$ is right-angled at $O$, so $OM+ON-MN = 2r$, where $r$ is the inradius. The task is therefore to maximize $r$.

The incircle has center $(r,r)$ and radius $r$, and it is tangent to line $MN$. Line $MN$ passes through $P$, with the circle on the same side as $O$. This is possible only if $P$ lies on or outside the circle. So $r$ is largest when $P$ lies on the circle:

$$\left(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}-r\right)^2+\left(\tfrac12-r\right)^2=r^2 \;\Rightarrow\; r^2-(\sqrt3+1)r+1=0.$$

The roots are
$$r=\frac{(\sqrt3+1)\pm\sqrt{2\sqrt3}}{2}.$$

The larger root, about $2.30$, is rejected. For it, $P$ would lie on the arc of the circle facing $O$, so the tangent at $P$ would not give a valid line with the circle between $O$ and the line. The valid root is the smaller one, $r\approx 0.4355$.

For this $r$ the tangent at $P$ has $x$-intercept about $0.94$ and $y$-intercept about $6.28$. Both are positive, so $M$ and $N$ lie on the rays and the configuration is valid.

Therefore
$$\max(OM+ON-MN)=2r=1+\sqrt3-\sqrt{2\sqrt3}.$$

ANSWER: $1+\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2\sqrt{3}}$
